mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5% over a 3-month window signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 5% for 3 months, as measured in out-of-sample walk-forward tests.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY, as tested over the last three recessions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for two consecutive months indicates labor market stress, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative 20-day returns are observed when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two months, in at least three separate episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during periods of four consecutive months of INDPRO contraction below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 5-year averages signals a stagflationary environment, which increases both discount rates and cost pressures, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 5-year averages simultaneously, in at least three historical episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A strong and persistent increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average, combined with rising real personal savings (RSAFS), signals a constructive demand outlook, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA AND RSAFS > 12-month MA for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive when both HOUST and RSAFS are above their 12-month moving averages for three consecutive months, in at least three recoveries.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its trend for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during periods of five consecutive months where PAYEMS exceeds its trend.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months, regardless of monetary policy stance, predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months, in at least three non-recessionary periods.
